newsitem.title: LEBANON: Japanese Red Army suspects charged in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Japanese Red Army suspects charged in Beirut.

text.p: A Beirut prosecutor charged five Japanese Red Army suspects on Thursday with passport forgery and other offences carrying penalties of up to seven years hard labour, judicial sources said.

Prosecutor Abdallah Bitar charged the alleged guerrillas with possessing and using forged passports, forging Lebanese government official stamps, entering the country illegally and illegal residence, the sources said.

The case will now be handed to an investigative judge who will carry out investigations and either order the suspects to be tried or released, depending on whether there is sufficient evidence of guilt, the sources added.
Lebanon's decision to charge the suspects put an end to Tokyo's hope of quick extradition.

Japan originally hoped that Lebanon would quickly deport them to face trial in Japan on international charges, but the case became bogged down in confusion for nearly three weeks before Lebanon decided to try them itself for local offences.
There has been no official explanation for the confusion and delay, which has aroused criticism in Lebanon of the government and concern that ties with Japan might suffer.

Lebanon has still not announced the identities of the suspects although officials have said Japan has identified them as Red Army guerrillas Kozo Okamoto, 49, Masao Adachi, 57, Mariko Yamamoto, 56, Kazuo Tohira, 44, and Haruo Wako, 48.
Prosecutor General Adnan Addoum was expected to release the names of the suspects later on Thursday. He was also expected to set free three other detained Japanese.
The three were identified as Sei Harada, Moroshima Takayaki and Shamato Yushiyoki.
Japanese officials shortly met the detainees on Wednesday for the first time since they were arrested on February 15 but were not allowed to interrogate them.
The Red Army, founded in 1971, is allied to hardline anti-Israeli Palestinian factions. All five suspects are on the international wanted list on various charges.
